What retention rate does Table 2 report for station M-09? Please give the value with its unit and tell me which source you used.

resources.title: Capacity Limits of Phoneme Drift
resources.version_label: Version of Record, Studies in Computational Pragmatics (2023)

paragraphs: We study phoneme drift across five monitoring stations using a hierarchical model.
Authors: Chiara Valdés, Yusuf Ekstrom, Zara Yildiz, Lena Whitcombe. Published in Studies in Computational Pragmatics, 2023.
Table 2 reports the retention rate for each station.

sections: Abstract

We report retention rate measurements from five monitoring stations collected between 2021 and 2023. A pilot survey in 2018 had put the regional retention rate at 104.2 %; we find marked differences between upland and coastal sites.
1. Introduction
Earlier studies of phoneme drift relied on single-site records [1, 2]. A multi-site campaign makes it possible to separate local effects from regional trends [3].
2. Methods

Station metadata are listed in Table 1. Measurements follow the protocol of [3]. Values from the 2020 campaign are given in Table 3 for comparison and are not directly comparable with the 2023 campaign because the instruments changed.
3. Results
Table 2 reports the retention rate for each station in the 2023 campaign. The largest change relative to 2020 was observed at station R-31.
4. Discussion
The spread between stations exceeds the measurement uncertainty, which suggests that site conditions dominate. Longer records are needed to confirm the trend.
References
[1] Sørlie et al. (2017). [2] Sandoval and Petrenko (2019). [3] Navarro et al. (2020).
